label: Faction
summary: The faction that this county member belongs to.
details: Going by its name and return type, it hands back the faction that this county member (one row of a faction's county list in the factions window) belongs to. The game's own GUI files use the same name on other types to set the data context to a faction, but nothing in the input shows this exact type using it.

label: Member county
summary: The county title that is the faction member.
details: The factions window uses it as the data context for one row of a faction's county list. Vanilla texts then call GetName on it for the county's name, in the tooltip about popular opinion in that county and in the tooltip about peasants joining the faction.

label: County opinion
summary: The number for the popular opinion (what the people there think) in the county, as shown for this faction member.
details: A vanilla text prints it with a sign (the |=+ format), so it can be positive or negative. It is a whole number.

label: County opinion breakdown
summary: A block of text describing the county's popular opinion.
details: Vanilla puts it under the heading 'Popular opinion in' plus the county's name, in a tooltip of the factions window.

label: This county member
summary: The faction county member itself, handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name and by how other types use a function of the same name (for example passing a character's own object into a text function), it gives the object back so it can be passed on. Nothing in the input uses it on this type. The game documents nothing more.

label: This faction item
summary: The faction item itself, handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name, it gives the object back so it can be passed to other functions. The game's GUI passes the same name on the widget type (PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf) to event window functions, but nothing in the input uses it on this type.

label: Are members visible
summary: Whether the member list of this faction entry is currently shown.
details: The factions window uses it to show or hide a part of an entry. Going by its name and that use, it tells if the entry is expanded.

label: Join tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for the button that joins this faction.
details: The factions window sets it as the tooltip of the join button.

label: Leave tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for the button that leaves this faction.
details: The factions window sets it as the tooltip of the leave button.

label: Press demands tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for the button that presses the faction's demands.
details: The factions window sets it as the tooltip of that button. The button's click function is spelled FactionItem.PressDemmands in the game.

label: Can join faction
summary: Whether the player can join this faction.
details: The factions window uses it to switch the join button on or off.

label: Can leave faction
summary: Whether the player can leave this faction.
details: The factions window uses it to switch the leave button on or off.

label: Can press demands
summary: Whether the player can press this faction's demands.
details: The factions window uses it to switch the press-demands button on or off.

label: Character members
summary: The list of characters who are members of this faction.
details: The factions window uses it as the list behind the character part of a faction entry. It is a list for the GUI to repeat a row over, not a single value.

label: County members
summary: The list of counties that are members of this faction.
details: The factions window uses it as the list behind the county part of a faction entry. It is a list for the GUI to repeat a row over, not a single value.

label: Discontent
summary: The faction's current discontent (how unhappy its members are) as a number.
details: Vanilla shows it as a percentage with no decimals next to the word discontent.

label: Target discontent
summary: A number for the discontent level the faction is heading toward.
details: Going by its name and its return type (a fixed-point number, like GetDiscontent), it is the value current discontent moves toward. Vanilla texts and GUI files do not use it. The game documents nothing more.

label: Discontent target position
summary: A screen position for the marker of the discontent target on the faction's bar.
details: Going by its name, it is a GUI position. Vanilla texts and GUI files do not use it. The game documents nothing more.

label: Discontent threshold position
summary: A screen position for the marker of the discontent threshold on the faction's bar.
details: Going by its name, it is a GUI position. Vanilla texts and GUI files do not use it. The game documents nothing more.

label: Discontent tooltip
summary: The tooltip text that explains the faction's discontent.
details: The factions window sets it as the tooltip of the discontent display.

label: Faction
summary: The faction this entry stands for.
details: The factions window uses it as the data context of an entry, so the parts inside can read the faction's own functions.

label: Max discontent
summary: A number for the highest discontent the faction can reach.
details: Going by its name, it is the upper limit of the discontent bar. Vanilla texts and GUI files do not use it. The game documents nothing more.

label: Members text
summary: A ready-made text shown on the button that opens or closes the faction's member list.
details: The factions window shows it as the button text in three places. Going by its name, it is the text about the members, and it is a ready-made text, not a number.

label: Months until max discontent
summary: The number of months until the faction's discontent reaches its maximum.
details: Vanilla uses it in the sentence 'Can send an Ultimatum in N months', so reaching the maximum is when the faction can send its ultimatum.

label: Faction power
summary: The faction's military power.
details: The factions window shows it as a percentage with no decimals, with value colouring, next to a 'military power' label.

label: Power fill
summary: A decimal that sets how far the faction's power bar is filled.
details: The factions window uses it as the value of two progress bars whose maximum is 1, so a full bar is 1. Which of the two bars shows depends on the threshold checks.

label: Power threshold position
summary: A screen position for the marker of the power threshold on the faction's power bar.
details: The factions window uses it as the position of the threshold marker icon on the power bar; the marker is shown only when IsPowerThresholdVisible is true.

label: Power tooltip
summary: The tooltip text that explains the faction's power.
details: The factions window sets it as the tooltip of the power display.

label: Show members tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for the button that shows or hides the faction's members.
details: The factions window uses it in three places.

label: Show members frame
summary: A whole number: which frame of the show/hide members button's picture to draw.
details: The factions window uses it as the frame of an icon in three places. Going by its name and use, it changes with whether the member list is open.

label: Has character members
summary: Whether the faction has any characters as members.
details: The factions window uses it to show or hide the character member part of an entry.

label: Has county members
summary: Whether the faction has any counties as members.
details: The factions window uses it to show or hide the county member part of an entry.

label: Has enough power
summary: Whether the faction's power has reached its threshold.
details: The factions window uses it together with IsPowerThresholdVisible to pick which of two displays to show. The meaning of the threshold itself comes from its name, not from the input.

label: Is discontent at max
summary: Whether the faction's discontent has reached its maximum.
details: The factions window then shows the text 'Can send an Ultimatum at any time'. If the discontent is neither at the maximum nor increasing, it shows 'Too weak to send an Ultimatum' instead.

label: Is discontent decreasing
summary: Whether the faction's discontent is going down.
details: The factions window uses it to show a trend arrow (the second frame of the arrow icon) next to the discontent label.

label: Is discontent increasing
summary: Whether the faction's discontent is going up.
details: The factions window uses it to show a trend arrow (the first frame of the arrow icon) and the line 'Can send an Ultimatum in N months'.

label: Is discontent threshold visible
summary: Whether the discontent threshold marker should be shown.
details: Going by its name, it controls a marker on the discontent bar. Vanilla texts and GUI files do not use it. The game documents nothing more.

label: Is player the leader
summary: Whether the player is the leader of this faction.
details: The factions window uses it, together with a check that the faction is not at war, to show the button that presses the demands.

label: Is player a member
summary: Whether the player is a member of this faction.
details: The factions window uses it to show the right buttons: for example a dangerous faction the player is not in, or a member who is not the leader.

label: Is power threshold visible
summary: Whether the faction's power threshold marker should be shown.
details: The factions window uses it to show or hide the marker, and combines it with HasEnoughPower.

label: Join faction
summary: Makes the player join this faction. Used as a button click.
details: The factions window runs it when the join button is clicked. It returns nothing.

label: Leave faction
summary: Makes the player leave this faction. Used as a button click.
details: The factions window runs it when the leave button is clicked. It returns nothing.

label: Press demands
summary: Presses the faction's demands on the ruler. Used as a button click.
details: The factions window runs it when the press-demands button is clicked. The game spells it PressDemmands, with a typo; write it exactly like that. It returns nothing.

label: This faction item
summary: The faction item itself, handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name and by how other types use a function of the same name (for example passing a character's own object into a text function), it gives the object back. Nothing in the input uses it on this type. The game documents nothing more.

label: Show cannot join
summary: Whether to show the 'cannot join' marker for this faction.
details: The factions window uses it to show a cross icon named cannot_join. It also uses it, with the 'my factions' and 'targeting factions' tab markers, to pick which of two show-members buttons appears.

label: Show or hide members
summary: Opens or closes the member list of this faction entry. Used as a button click.
details: The factions window runs it on click in three places. Going by its name and use, it toggles the list. It returns nothing.

label: Show join button
summary: Whether the join button should be shown for this faction.
details: The factions window uses it to show or hide the button.

label: Show potential members
summary: Opens the add-members view of this faction. Used as a button click.
details: The factions window runs it on click of the 'Add Members' button, which is shown only when the player is a member; its tooltip is titled 'Force Characters to Join'. Going by that, it is for adding members by force. It returns nothing.

label: This factions window
summary: The factions window itself, handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name, it gives the window object back so it can be passed to other functions. Nothing in the input uses it on this type.

label: Can create any faction
summary: Whether the player can create at least one kind of faction.
details: The factions window shows one part when it is true and another when it is false.

label: Can join any faction
summary: Whether the player can join at least one faction.
details: The factions window shows one part when it is true and another when it is false.

label: Close window
summary: Closes the factions window. Used as a button click.
details: The window's close button runs it. It returns nothing. The same name Close appears on many other window types (260 uses in all).

label: Vassals who cannot join
summary: The list of vassals who cannot create or join a faction.
details: The factions window uses it as a list to repeat a row over.

label: Faction types to create
summary: The list of entries for the kinds of faction that can be created.
details: The factions window uses it as a list to repeat a row over; each entry says whether it is shown and whether the player can create it.

label: Joinable factions
summary: The list of factions the player could join.
details: The factions window uses it as a list to repeat a row over.

label: Joined factions
summary: The list of factions the player is a member of.
details: The factions window uses it as a list to repeat a row over.

label: Members available to force
summary: The number of characters who could be forced to join the faction.
details: Vanilla shows it in the 'Add Members (N)' button and in its tooltip titled 'Force Characters to Join'.

label: Factions targeting the player
summary: The list of factions that are aimed at the player.
details: The factions window uses it as a list in its 'targeting factions' tab, whose icon is named faction_against_you. That is why it is read as the factions against the player.

label: Has targeting factions
summary: Whether any faction is aimed at the player.
details: The factions window shows the list when it is true and another part of the window when it is false.

label: Has vassals who cannot join
summary: Whether there are vassals who cannot create or join a faction.
details: Going by its name and its sibling GetCantCreateOrJoinFactionVassals, it tells if that list has anything in it. Vanilla texts and GUI files do not use it. The game documents nothing more.

label: Is in any faction
summary: Whether the player belongs to at least one faction.
details: The factions window hides its tab buttons when the player is an independent ruler and in no faction. It also uses it to choose between the list of joined factions and the other part.

label: Is my factions tab selected
summary: Whether the 'my factions' tab is the open tab.
details: Going by its name, it checks the tab choice. Vanilla texts and GUI files do not use it. The game documents nothing more.

label: Is primary title titular
summary: Whether the player's primary title is a titular one.
details: The factions window uses it, with a check that the player's government is not ecclesiastical, to decide whether to show one part of the window. What 'titular' means is the game's own term; the input does not explain it.

label: Is targeting tab selected
summary: Whether the 'targeting factions' tab is the open tab.
details: Going by its name, it checks the tab choice. Vanilla texts and GUI files do not use it. The game documents nothing more.

label: This factions window
summary: The factions window itself, handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name and by how a function of the same name is used on other types (passing the object into a text function), it gives the object back. Nothing in the input uses it on this type.

label: Show my factions
summary: Switches the factions window to the 'my factions' tab.
details: Going by its name, it is meant as a click action. Vanilla texts and GUI files do not use it. It returns nothing.

label: Show targeting factions
summary: Switches the factions window to the 'targeting factions' tab.
details: Going by its name, it is meant as a click action. Vanilla texts and GUI files do not use it. It returns nothing.

label: This faith
summary: The faith itself, handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name, it gives the object back so it can be passed to other functions. The input shows the same name used only on the widget type, not on a faith.

label: Alternative priest term (plural)
summary: The faith's alternative word for its priests, in the plural.
details: Going by its name, it is the faith's alternative word for priests. Vanilla uses it in decision texts, for example 'Restore the [it]' and 'Call the [it] to the river'.

label: Female bishop title
summary: The faith's word for a female bishop.
details: Vanilla uses it in a custom text that gives the bishop title of the character's faith. Add |U to capitalise the first letter.

label: Female bishop title (plural)
summary: The faith's word for female bishops, in the plural.
details: Vanilla uses it in a custom text for the bishop title of the character's faith.

label: Male bishop title
summary: The faith's word for a male bishop.
details: Vanilla uses it in a custom text that gives the bishop title of the character's faith.

label: Male bishop title (plural)
summary: The faith's word for male bishops, in the plural.
details: Vanilla uses it in a custom text for the bishop title of the character's faith.

label: Neutral bishop title
summary: The faith's gender-neutral word for a bishop.
details: Vanilla uses it in a custom text for the bishop title of the character's faith.

label: Neutral bishop title (plural)
summary: The faith's gender-neutral word for bishops, in the plural.
details: Vanilla uses it in a custom text for the bishop title of the character's faith.

label: Can start find-adherent scheme
summary: Whether the player can start a scheme to find a character of this faith.
details: The faith window uses it, with two checks about the rite shown, to decide whether to show the find-adherent part. The tooltip text on that button reads 'Start a scheme to find a [adherent]'.

label: Creator: her/him
summary: The pronoun 'her' or 'him' for the faith's creator.
details: Going by its name and its use inside event and decision texts, it picks the object pronoun that fits the creator deity.

label: Creator: her/his
summary: The pronoun 'her' or 'his' for the faith's creator.
details: Vanilla uses it in a decision text: 'Our creator [name] made us in [it] image'. Add |U to capitalise it.

label: Creator name
summary: The name of the faith's creator deity.
details: Vanilla uses it in decision and event texts, for example 'Our creator [name] made us'.

label: Creator name (possessive)
summary: The name of the faith's creator deity in the possessive form (name's).
details: Going by its name and its use in event texts. It is a text for the faith's creator.

label: Creator: she/he
summary: The pronoun 'she' or 'he' for the faith's creator.
details: Going by its name and its sibling functions CreatorHerHim and CreatorHerHis. Vanilla texts do not use it. The game documents nothing more.

label: Custom text
summary: The text that a custom localization entry produces for the faith.
details: It takes one argument, the key of a custom localization written for faiths, such as `Custom('CoronationRequiresArtifact')`. The entry picks its text by its triggers; that one names the kind of artifact (a crown, regalia or either) the faith's coronation needs.

fields.name: key
fields.values: the key of a custom localization of type faith, in quotes

label: Custom localization
summary: A text taken from a custom localization entry, with the faith as its subject.
details: Going by its name and type, it works like Custom. Vanilla texts do not use it. The game documents nothing more.

label: Death deity: her/him
summary: The pronoun 'her' or 'him' for the faith's death deity.
details: Going by its name and its use in one event text about a legend spreading.

label: Death deity: her/his
summary: The pronoun 'her' or 'his' for the faith's death deity.
details: Going by its name and use in event texts about plague.

label: Death deity name
summary: The name of the faith's god of death.
details: Vanilla uses it in texts about plague and war, for example 'my soul was challenged by [name]'. Add |U to capitalise it.

label: Death deity name (possessive)
summary: The name of the faith's god of death in the possessive form (name's).
details: Going by its name and use in event texts.

label: Death deity: she/he
summary: The pronoun 'she' or 'he' for the faith's death deity.
details: Vanilla uses it at the start of a sentence in a legend event ('[it|U] has marked me with this visit').

label: Devil: her/his
summary: The pronoun 'her' or 'his' for the faith's devil figure.
details: Vanilla uses it in a legend text about bandits and evildoers.

label: Devil: herself/himself
summary: The reflexive pronoun 'herself' or 'himself' for the faith's devil figure.
details: Going by its name and use in event texts.

label: Devil name
summary: The name of the faith's devil figure (its evil adversary).
details: Vanilla uses it in legend texts, for example about a hero haunted by visions of it.

label: Devil name (possessive)
summary: The name of the faith's devil figure in the possessive form (name's).
details: Going by its name and use in event texts.

label: Devil: she/he
summary: The pronoun 'she' or 'he' for the faith's devil figure.
details: Going by its name and its use in a childhood event text.

label: Female devotee term
summary: The faith's word for a female devotee (a pious follower).
details: Vanilla uses it in custom texts that give the devotee title of the character's faith. Add |U to capitalise it.

label: Female devotee term (plural)
summary: The faith's word for female devotees, in the plural.
details: Vanilla uses it in custom texts for the devotee title of the character's faith.

label: Male devotee term
summary: The faith's word for a male devotee (a pious follower).
details: Vanilla uses it in custom texts that give the devotee title of the character's faith.

label: Male devotee term (plural)
summary: The faith's word for male devotees, in the plural.
details: Vanilla uses it in custom texts for the devotee title of the character's faith.

label: Neutral devotee term
summary: The faith's gender-neutral word for a devotee.
details: Vanilla uses it in a fallback custom text for the devotee title.

label: Neutral devotee term (plural)
summary: The faith's gender-neutral word for devotees, in the plural.
details: Going by its name and its use in decision texts.

label: Divine realm
summary: The name the faith gives its divine realm.
details: Vanilla uses it in a holy order name 'Guardians of [it]'.

label: Divine realm (second name)
summary: A second name for the faith's divine realm.
details: Going by its name and its sibling DivineRealm. Vanilla texts do not use it. The game documents nothing more.

label: Divine realm (third name)
summary: A third name for the faith's divine realm.
details: Going by its name and its sibling DivineRealm. Vanilla texts do not use it. The game documents nothing more.

label: Evil god names
summary: The names of the faith's evil gods.
details: Vanilla uses it in event texts, for example 'I'll warn them about [it]!' and 'consorting with [it]'.

label: Fate god: her/him
summary: The pronoun 'her' or 'him' for the faith's god of fate.
details: Going by its name and its siblings. Vanilla texts do not use it. The game documents nothing more.

label: Fate god: her/his
summary: The pronoun 'her' or 'his' for the faith's god of fate.
details: Going by its name and its siblings. Vanilla texts do not use it. The game documents nothing more.

label: Fate god name
summary: The name of the faith's god of fate (luck).
details: Vanilla uses it in event texts about chance, for example a board game line 'By [name], you're as bad at it as you are at ruling' and 'sometimes [name] smiles upon a man'.

label: Fate god name (possessive)
summary: The name of the faith's god of fate in the possessive form (name's).
details: Going by its name and its use in board game event texts.

label: Fate god: she/he
summary: The pronoun 'she' or 'he' for the faith's god of fate.
details: Going by its name and its use in event texts about luck.

label: Fertility god: her/him
summary: The pronoun 'her' or 'him' for the faith's god of fertility.
details: Going by its name and its siblings. Vanilla texts do not use it. The game documents nothing more.

label: Fertility god: her/his
summary: The word "her" or "his" for the faith's god of fertility.
details: Vanilla uses it in a pilgrimage event text after the god's name ("... in all her beauty"), reached through the global GetFaithByKey. The game lists no return type.

label: Fertility god name
summary: The name of the faith's god of fertility.
details: Vanilla uses it to build the name of a rite and its adjective, with a suffix added to the name.

label: Fertility god name (possessive)
summary: The name of the faith's god of fertility in the possessive form (name's).
details: Going by its name and its use in an alms text.

label: Fertility god: she/he
summary: The pronoun 'she' or 'he' for the faith's god of fertility.
details: Going by its name and its siblings. Vanilla texts do not use it. The game documents nothing more.

label: Great Holy War name
summary: The faith's name for a Great Holy War (a faith's large religious war).
details: Vanilla uses it after the faith's adjective, for example 'My [adjective] [it] for [title]'.

label: Great Holy War name (plural)
summary: The faith's name for Great Holy Wars, in the plural.
details: Going by its name and its use in faith creation and war event texts.

label: Active clerical electors
summary: The list of clerical electors of the faith who are active.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla texts and GUI files do not use it. The game documents nothing more.

label: Adherent name
summary: The faith's word for one of its followers, as text with a hover tooltip.
details: Vanilla uses it with GetFaithByKey in council task, decision and event texts, such as converting others or "If you are already of ... faith".

label: Adherent name (no tooltip)
summary: The faith's word for one follower, as plain text.
details: Vanilla uses it in 'Start a scheme to find a [it]' and as the faith name of a rite.

label: Adherent name (plural)
summary: The faith's word for its followers, in the plural, with a tooltip.
details: Vanilla uses it in memory texts about holy wars, after the faith's adjective.

label: Adherent name (plural, no tooltip)
summary: The faith's word for its followers, in the plural, as plain text.
details: Vanilla uses it in legend texts about priesthood being restored.

label: Adjective
summary: The faith's adjective (for example the word before 'crusade'), with a tooltip.
details: Vanilla uses it a great many times, in front of a noun like the war name. The NoTooltip form gives plain text.

label: Adjective (no tooltip)
summary: The faith's adjective, as plain text.
details: Vanilla uses it to build faction names like 'Culture Faith-adjective Populists'.

label: Base spiritual fulfillment
summary: A number for the base spiritual fulfillment of the faith.
details: Going by its name and its return type. Vanilla texts and GUI files do not use it. The game documents nothing more.

label: Challengers
summary: The list of challengers shown in the faith window.
details: Each entry has a challenger title with a holder, so they are people, not faiths. The window shows them in the head-of-faith area, counts them with the 'Challengers' label and shows a button only when the list is not empty. Who exactly they challenge comes from the concept key challenger_hof, not from the input.

label: College election title
summary: The title that the faith's clerical college elects (as the faith's electoral title).
details: The HUD asks it whether it has the theocratic elective election type, together with a check that the faith has clerical electors. It is a title, so title functions work on it.

label: Core tenet background icon
summary: The background icon for the faith's core tenet.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla texts and GUI files do not use it. The game documents nothing more.

label: Counties change
summary: The net number of counties the faith will gain (positive) or lose (negative).
details: The ledger tooltip says the faith 'will gain' when the number is above -1, otherwise 'lose'. Below it the tooltip lists the gains and losses (GetCountiesGain, GetCountiesLoss) on their own. It is a whole number.

label: Counties gained
summary: The number of counties that are being converted to this faith.
details: The ledger tooltip lists it as counties being converted to the faith. The same tooltip uses GetCountiesLoss for the opposite direction.

label: Counties lost
summary: The number of this faith's counties that are being converted to another faith.
details: The ledger tooltip lists it that way. The same tooltip uses GetCountiesGain for the opposite direction.

label: Default theocracy government
summary: The government type that is the faith's default theocracy.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla texts and GUI files do not use it. The game documents nothing more.

label: Defensive Great Holy Wars
summary: The list of Great Holy Wars in which the faith is defending.
details: The HUD uses it as a list, called on the player's faith.

label: Description
summary: The faith's description text.
details: Going by its name and its type. The input shows the same name used on other types only, so this is a hint, not proof.

label: Doctrines
summary: The list of the faith's doctrines.
details: The faith window uses it as a list to repeat a row over.

label: Eminent holy sites
summary: The list of the faith's eminent holy sites.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla texts and GUI files do not use it. The game documents nothing more.

label: Fervor
summary: The faith's fervor as a number.
details: Vanilla shows it as a percentage, with no decimals in the window and two in the tooltip. The tooltip says the effects of fervor are always relative to the opposing faith's fervor.

label: Fervor changelog
summary: A text that lists what changed the faith's fervor.
details: Vanilla uses it in the fervor tooltip.

label: Flavor description
summary: The faith's flavor text, a short descriptive text.
details: Vanilla uses it as the description text of a rite and in a tooltip.

label: Founder
summary: The character who founded the faith.
details: Going by its name. The input shows the same name only on other types, so this is a hint, not proof.

label: Great Holy War
summary: The Great Holy War the faith is taking part in.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context in the HUD and for the war's name in a rich-presence status line ('Fighting in the [name]').

label: Heresy threshold
summary: The rite divergence number above which a rite of the faith may be branded heretical.
details: Vanilla shows it in the rite windows as the heretical threshold, in texts like 'divergence at or over [it] - Heretical Rite' and 'goes over [it], it may be branded as heretical'.

label: Holy sites
summary: The list of the faith's holy sites.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla texts and GUI files do not use it. The game documents nothing more.

label: Hostility level towards
summary: How hostile this faith is toward another faith.
details: Going by its name. It takes two arguments, which the input does not describe. Vanilla texts and GUI files do not use it. The game documents nothing more.

label: ID
summary: The faith's internal number.
details: Vanilla compares it with the player's faith ID to tell whether two faiths are the same.

label: Icon
summary: The faith's icon picture.
details: The HUD uses it as a texture, so it can be drawn as an image.

label: Inactive clerical electors
summary: The list of clerical electors of the faith who are inactive.
details: Going by its name and its sibling GetActiveClericalElectors. Vanilla texts and GUI files do not use it. The game documents nothing more.

label: Faith or religion label
summary: A text label that says whether to call it a faith or a religion.
details: Going by its name and its text return type. Vanilla texts and GUI files do not use it. The game documents nothing more.

label: Main rite
summary: The faith's main rite.
details: Vanilla passes it to the tenet type's GetName in texts about a faith adopting a tenet.

label: Name
summary: The faith's name, with a tooltip.
details: Used very often (18920 uses in vanilla), for example in memory texts about a faith someone abandoned. GetNameNoTooltip gives plain text.

label: Name (no tooltip)
summary: The faith's name, as plain text.
details: Vanilla uses it in legend texts and as the heading of the faith window.

label: Controlled holy sites
summary: The number of the faith's holy sites that its followers control.
details: The ledger shows it as 'controlled / total', next to the faith's total number of holy sites.
